verdict.reasoning: Patient reports sudden left-sided headache with visual changes: 'So, it started in the morning... my vision is a little bit blurred... some zigzag lines' and 'It's in uh, one side, uh, the left side, only.' Doctor confirms sudden onset: 'was it a sudden onset headache...?' Patient: 'Yeah, yeah, yeah.'

Headache onset and duration: Doctor: 'This morning... about four hours ago, you've developed a headache?' Patient: 'Yep.' Sudden onset: Patient answered 'Yeah, yeah, yeah' to 'was it a sudden onset headache'.

Blurred vision with zigzag lines and screen intolerance: Patient: 'My vision is quite blurred... it's really weird, like some zigzag lines.' and later 'I feel a little bit, a little bit better. , I cannot stand screens.'

Dizziness, nausea, vomiting twice, ongoing nausea: Patient: 'I feel like um, uh, dizzy.' 'Ohh yeah... definitely, I vomit twice.' 'as soon as the, the headache started, I also vomited... and I still feel nausea.' 'To be honest, I'm about to vomit, very soon, I think.' Doctor summarizes: 'you feel a bit nauseous, you vomited twice.'

Worse with movement and prefers head still: Patient: 'when I move, like the thing is that if I, if I leave bed, I start to feel like, even worse if I move.' and 'So, I just want to have my hay, my head like really, uh, not moving.'

Paracetamol timing and ineffectiveness: Patient: 'Yeah, I tried Paracetemol, but uh, didn't work. To be honest, I feel exactly the same.' and 'the headache started like... four hours ago. So, I would say like, maybe three hours ago, because I couldn't stand it.'

First headache of this type: Doctor: 'Have you ever had a headache like this in the past?' Patient: 'Um, well not, really.' and 'Like this, I, yeah, like this, no, definitely. It's something new.' Doctor: 'So, it's a first .'

Denies limb weakness and gait disturbance: Doctor: 'have you noticed any weakness in your arms or legs, anything like that?' Patient: 'No, no , no, no.' and 'when you're walking, you're able to walk fine in a straight line...?' Patient: 'Uh, not really.' Doctor then summarizes: 'you've got no neurological symptoms. You're walking fine.'
History of kidney stones: Patient: 'Well, I had the kidney stone, so let's say that that's ten.' Doctor: 'You've mentioned, in the past, you've had kidney stones, any other medical problems?'
Mother has migraines and hypothyroidism: Patient: 'my mother has migraines.' and later 'also, I have hypothyroidism in the family.' then clarifies 'She also has Hypothyroidism.'
No regular medications: Doctor: 'And do you take any regular medications?' Patient: 'Uh, no.'
No known drug allergies: Doctor: 'Are you allergic to any medications?' Patient: 'Not that I'm aware, uh... Yeah, not that I'm aware.' This corresponds to NKDA.
Pregnancy unlikely: Doctor: 'Is there any chance you could be pregnant?' Patient: 'Uh, I really doubt it.'

Anxious about tumor/stroke and A&E: Patient: 'I feel that this can be some kind of brain tumour... or maybe a stroke.' and 'you definitely start wonder, if i should go to A and E urgently, because , I might really have something serious.'

Probable migraine with visual aura, unilateral headache, blurred zigzag vision, nausea, vomiting, paracetamol ineffective: Doctor: 'So, it sounds like what you're suffering from is what's known as a migraine.' He cites 'on one side of the head... you've got blurry vision... with the nausea and vomiting.' Patient previously described 'zigzag lines' and 'Paracetemol... didn't work.' Visual phenomena are consistent with aura.

Planned trial of ibuprofen, antiemetic, sugary carbonated drink: Doctor: 'I would recommend... if you take some medications, maybe something like ibuprofen?' and later 'there's, it can be ibuprofen with an anti-sickness, um, so and , which you can get from the pharmacy. Um, and you also to drink, uh, sugary and carbonated drinks, something like Coke.'

Counseling on relief time and migraine duration: Doctor: 'we can look at maybe half an hour to forty minutes, depending on what your response to it is' and 'they can last from anywhere from four hours to seventy two hours, migraines can last.'

Same-day in-person review for neuro exam unless resolved, cancel if improved: Doctor: 'we would want to see you, um, as soon as possible, to do like a full neurological exam as well.' and later 'assessment to where we can see you today at some point.' and 'if you do take these medications and... you feel much better in yourself, you can cancel it, um, you can give us a call and cancel it.'

Advice to contact clinic if no improvement or worsening: Doctor: 'any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.' This covers contacting for earlier review or if symptoms worsen.
